messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, Based on the current docs, the go‑live/acceptance rules are defined at a high level only – there is no detailed matrix by method/scheme/issuer. 1) Acceptance rule: counts, caps, required test cases
From the go‑live and verification flows:
- Minimum requirement: - Perform at least one successful production transaction and - Share the production transaction ID and supporting evidence (screenshots/video) so Integration can verify settlement + check‑transaction/callback. - If cards are in scope, the docs say this is typically a card transaction.
- Amount level: - Repeatedly described as a small/low‑value transaction, if agreed.
- Per‑method / per‑issuer / per‑scheme counts: - Not specified. The docs do not define a required number of transactions per method (ABA PAY, KHQR, card, UPI, Alipay, WeChat, etc.) or per issuer/scheme. - For multi‑outlet deployments, Integration may request at least one transaction per outlet to verify settlement mapping.
- Required test cases: - At go‑live, focus is on verifying: - End‑to‑end payment success flow - Settlement mapping to the correct account - Check Transaction API / callback behavior - There is no documented, fixed list of mandatory test cases per payment method/scheme/issuer (e.g. specific issuer combinations or card brands) in the KB. So formally in the docs: ≥1 successful prod transaction (card if available), small value, plus evidence for settlement & callback/Check‑Transaction verification. Anything more granular is internal policy, not described here. 2) Mandatory cases (refund, capture, CoF, payout)
The go‑live flows in the KB do not list any of the following as universally mandatory for initial production acceptance:
- Refund flows
- Pre‑auth + capture/void
- Credentials‑on‑File (CIT/MIT) flows
- Payout/disbursement flows They focus instead on:
- At least one successful production payment
- Evidence for settlement and transaction‑status logic (Check Transaction / callback) Which advanced flows must be proven before go‑live (refund, pre‑auth, CoF, payout) is not standardised in the KB; it’s treated as scope‑ and contract‑dependent, to be defined between the merchant and the Integration/Commercial teams. 3) Restricted customer traffic before first settlement verification
From the documented flows:
- Sequence is: 1. Integration completed in sandbox. 2. Production credentials issued. 3. Merchant performs at least one production transaction. 4. Merchant shares transaction ID + evidence. 5. Integration verifies settlement & technical behavior. 6. Merchant profile is marked live / expiry removed, and VIP support starts.
- Some texts mention the “first live transaction (or flagged transactions)” may be reviewed and may require supporting documents, which implies that the first production transaction can be a real customer payment in practice.
- However, the KB does not explicitly state a rule like “restricted live traffic is allowed before settlement verification under conditions X/Y” nor any formal cap or volume threshold for such traffic. So, per documentation:
- Official go‑live status and removal of temporary restrictions only happen after at least one production transaction is verified for settlement.
- Whether a merchant may start restricted/soft‑launch customer traffic before that verification is not codified in the KB and would need to be agreed with Integration/Commercial/Compliance on a case‑by‑case basis. For exact current acceptance criteria (per‑method counts, any mandatory refund/pre‑auth/CoF/payout tests, and rules around soft‑launch traffic), you’d need to align with the internal Integration and Merchant Support policies, as they’re not fully specified in the external docs.

messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, Based on the docs we have: 1) API/schema/portal view for per‑profile capabilities - Payment methods and capabilities (KHQR, ABA PAY, cards, Alipay, WeChat, etc.) are configured per merchant profile in PayWay’s backend. - Integrators are instructed to obtain the allowed payment methods from the ABA PayWay Integration Team and configure their UI/integration accordingly. - There is no documented public API or versioned “describe profile” schema that returns: - which payment methods are enabled, - which currencies, or - which capabilities (refund, pre‑auth, tokenization, etc.) are enabled. - A merchant portal/admin may show some configuration, but the KB treats PayWay backend + Integration Team confirmation as the authoritative source, not a discoverable API. 2) Currencies - Each merchant profile has a single settlement currency configured; it does not support multiple currencies per profile. - There is no API described that returns a currency matrix per method. Currency is part of the profile configuration, confirmed with the Integration/Commercial teams. 3) Capabilities (refund, pre‑auth, tokenization) - These are governed by profile setup + contract (e.g., whether card processing, KHQR, pre‑auth, KHQR API, etc. are enabled). - Docs mention that trying to use unsupported operations leads to errors (e.g., “Selected Payment Option is not enabled for this Merchant Profile”, or pre‑auth operations failing if the transaction wasn’t created as pre‑auth), but they do not specify a capability‑discovery endpoint. 4) Programmatic verification vs inference From the KB, there is no supported, dedicated introspection API to programmatically list “these methods/capabilities are enabled on this profile”. The recommended approach is:
- Design‑time / configuration‑time: - Get the official list of enabled methods & capabilities from the ABA PayWay Integration/Commercial team per merchant profile and environment (sandbox, production). - Configure your app/plugin to only show and call those methods.
- Runtime: - Still handle configuration errors (e.g., “Selected Payment Option is not enabled for this Merchant Profile”) as hard signals that the profile is not configured for that option. So, per current documentation there is no general “profile capability schema/API”; enablement is confirmed via Integration/Commercial team + portal configuration, and in code you must rely on that static configuration and normal error handling rather than a formal capability‑discovery API.

messages.text:
Part 2/2 - In‑flight transaction at revocation time - The KB does not define special handling for a race where a charge is in flight exactly when the user revokes consent. - Practically per docs: - If the transaction was already authorised before token becomes invalid, it will complete/decline based on normal issuer/gateway rules. - Once the token is expired/frozen/removed, further attempts with that token are declined. - Merchants should: - Rely on Payment callbacks + transaction status checks for the definitive outcome of any in‑flight charge. - On receiving a token‑status change callback (freeze/remove/expire), immediately mark the related subscription or stored method as inactive and stop scheduling further MITs. - Retries and grace - Any retry policy (e.g. retry X times over Y days) is owned by the merchant. The KB does not define a PayWay‑managed retry/grace framework. - If you retry against a revoked/expired token, those attempts will just be declined; the gateway does not silently “queue” them or override the user’s revocation. ---
3) CIT vs MIT rules and when 3‑D Secure is required Yes – there are two main strands of documentation you can follow: - CIT vs MIT and token flags (CoF docs) - Unscheduled payments: - CITI_FLEX – Customer links a method for Customer‑Initiated variable‑amount payments. - CITU_FLEX – Subsequent CIT payments using that token. - CITO_FLEX – Customer authorises the merchant to initiate MIT variable‑amount payments later. - MITU_FLEX – Subsequent MIT payments using that token. - Scheduled payments: - CITR_FIX – Initial CIT registration for a fixed amount/frequency subscription. - MITR_FIX – Subsequent MIT recurring charges for that fixed plan. - Rules explicitly stated: - Tokens are restricted by Initiation Type: - CITI_FLEX tokens cannot be used for MIT payments. - CITO_FLEX tokens are intended for MIT scenarios. - 3‑D Secure requirements and behaviour - General 3DS rules: - Cards enrolled in 3D Secure require an OTP or equivalent customer authentication to complete a transaction. - Manual key‑in and card‑not‑present flows without customer authentication are not allowed for 3DS‑protected cards. - Card entry must use the PayWay‑hosted UI/iframe or hosted checkout; merchants must not capture raw card data themselves unless they are on a separate product with PCI‑DSS evidence. - Integration rules: - If a 3DS challenge is returned, your integration must surface the OTP/challenge to the cardholder and wait for the result before confirming payment. - 3DS prompts and some decline reasons are controlled by the issuer and card network; some cards may be non‑3DS or not participating. If your merchant profile requires 3DS, such cards are rejected. - For saved‑card (CoF) flows that require OTP, PayWay/bank‑side flows handle the 3DS challenge where applicable. - Declines & issuer rules: - Issuing banks can enforce their own rules (daily limits, risk flags), which may cause declines even when 3DS is passed. - For troubleshooting, you’re expected to capture the gateway/issuer response codes and work with the issuer if needed. These docs (Credentials‑on‑File: Unscheduled & Scheduled Payments + the 3D Secure / card entry rule + decline/3DS FAQ) form the current reference set for CIT/MIT modelling and 3DS expectations in PayWay.

[Part 1/2]
Hello Bong @Ruzaid,
**1) Consent, audit/retenti…
messages.text:
[Part 1/2] Hello Bong @Ruzaid, **1) Consent, audit/retention rules, and who owns the schedule** From the Credentials‑on‑File and Scheduled/Unscheduled Payment docs:
- **Consent model** - *Scheduled payments* (subscriptions) use **CITR_FIX → MITR_FIX**: - Customer performs a **CITR_FIX** “Subscribe” transaction where they explicitly agree to a **fixed amount & frequency** (e.g. $20/month gym plan). - PayWay generates a **payment token (PWT)** and pushes it to the merchant via `callback_url`. - *Unscheduled payments* (variable amount, not on a schedule) use **CITI_FLEX / CITO_FLEX → CITU_FLEX / MITU_FLEX**: - Customer links an ABA account/card via **Link Account / Link Card** with the appropriate `token_flag` to authorize **customer‑initiated** (CIT) or **merchant‑initiated** (MIT) future payments. - Merchants **must provide UI** to: - **Subscribe/Link** (obtain consent), - **View** subscriptions/payment methods (merchant name, amount, frequency), - **Unsubscribe / Remove** methods. - Customers also have full control from **ABA Mobile** to **freeze, unfreeze, renew or remove** tokens. - **Audit & retention** - PayWay stores the **token + masked source_of_fund** and token metadata (`expired_at`, `token_flag`, `status`, limits, currency). - Merchants store: - The **token (`pwt`)**, - Their internal **ctid/customer ID**, - Subscription/config data (plan, amount, frequency, next charge date) in their own system. - Rules: - **Expired tokens cannot be used**: any payment attempt with an expired token is declined; customer gets an ABA Mobile notification. - **Frozen/removed tokens cannot be used**: requests will be declined and customers are notified. - Merchants **must not store raw card PAN/CVV** – card entry happens on PayWay‑hosted UI, and only tokens/masked details are stored by the merchant. - **Who owns the charge schedule?** - For **scheduled payments**: - Docs are explicit that **“every day, the Merchant Server runs a scheduled job”** to find due subscriptions and call the **Payment API** with the stored token. - So **the merchant owns the schedule, logic, and retry strategy**. - PayWay only processes a charge **when the merchant calls the API**; it does not autonomously run the billing schedule. - For **unscheduled payments**, the merchant/app decides **when** to trigger CIT or MIT payments using the token (subject to token limits/status and scheme/issuer rules). ---
**2) Revoked consent, in‑flight charges, retries & grace periods** - **How revocation happens** - On the merchant side: customer **unsubscribes** / removes a payment method in the merchant UI; the merchant then stops scheduling further charges. - On the bank side (ABA Mobile): the user can **freeze**, **unfreeze**, **renew**, or **remove** a token. - Token status values: - `1` = active - `2` = frozen - `0` = removed - **Effect on new/future charges** - For **expired tokens**: any subsequent transaction is **declined**; ABA Mobile notifies the user that the payment method is no longer valid. - For **frozen or removed tokens**: any transaction attempt using that token is **declined**, and ABA Mobile informs the user that the selected method is inactive/frozen/removed. - There is **no “grace period” documented** once the token is expired/frozen/removed – gateway behaviour is simply to decline.

1) Google Pay availability & enablement…
messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, 1) Google Pay availability & enablement From the documentation available here:
- The supported methods for PayWay payment links/online checkout are listed as ABA Pay, card payments (Visa/MasterCard/JCB), UPI, KHQR, WeChat Pay, Alipay. - It explicitly notes that “Google Pay for online transactions was not available at the time of the discussion.” - There is no environment-specific matrix (sandbox vs production) showing Google Pay as enabled, nor any enablement procedure for it. So based on this KB, Google Pay is not documented as an available online method in any environment, and there is no described onboarding flow for it. Given your SDK exposes a google_pay option, you’d need confirmation from the PayWay Integration/Sales team whether this is now live or still not enabled in gateway, and what the current enablement process is. 2) Per-method currency matrix & fee schedule The materials here do not include a current matrix of:
- supported currencies per method (ABA PAY, KHQR, cards incl. UnionPay/JCB/UPI, Alipay, WeChat), nor
- per-method fee/commission schedules. Those are handled as commercial/contractual terms per merchant. For an authoritative matrix and pricing, merchants must check their merchant agreement or contact PayWay Sales/Commercial (e.g. paywaysales@ababank.com / their account manager). 3) How a merchant can verify which methods are enabled on their profile From the integration-side docs, the recommended ways are: - Confirm with ABA PayWay Integration/Sales team - The Integration/Commercial team can list which methods are actually activated on the merchant profile in sandbox and production. - This is the canonical source and should be aligned with the merchant’s contract. - Merchant portal / admin view (where available) - Some setups expose enabled methods or toggles in the merchant portal/admin; merchants can see which options (e.g. KHQR, cards, Alipay/WeChat) are active there. - However, the docs emphasise that profile configuration in PayWay’s backend is authoritative, not just what’s ticked in a plugin UI. - Behaviour during integration tests - If a method is not enabled on the merchant profile, then even if it’s selected in the plugin or passed as payment_option, you typically see: - The method not appearing as a selectable option, or - An error such as “Selected Payment Option is not enabled for this Merchant Profile”, or similar failure, and the transaction won’t proceed. - For plugins (e.g., Shopify and others), the set of methods shown on the ABA PayWay hosted checkout page reflects what’s enabled on the merchant agreement; missing methods there usually mean they’re not enabled. So operationally: merchants should (a) confirm with the Integration/Sales team which methods are active, and (b) verify via sandbox tests that those methods appear and work as expected; plugin-side toggles alone are not sufficient if the profile backend doesn’t have the method enabled.

Hello Bong @Ruzaid,
1) Callback URL sharing between Custome…
messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, 1) Callback URL sharing between Customer Module vs online checkout
For the Customer Module there is only one callback URL per merchant profile:
- The docs state: “Callback URL: Only one URL; change requires support ticket.”
- That single URL is used for webhook notifications, regardless of channel.
➡️ You cannot provision a separate callback URL per channel; Customer Module and online-checkout callbacks go to the same profile callback URL and are distinguished by their payload/body. 2) Signature canonicalization vs online-checkout
Customer Module callbacks use the same hash model as online-checkout callbacks:
- Hash is computed over a sorted-key concatenation of the callback fields.
- Signature is sent in header X-PAYWAY-HMAC-SHA512.
➡️ Treat canonicalization the same as your online-checkout callback logic (sorted keys, consistent encoding of values) rather than introducing a Customer-Module–specific variant. 3) Algorithm: HMAC-SHA512 vs HMAC-SHA256
For Customer Module callbacks the docs are explicit:
- Callback hash: HMAC-SHA512, then Base64-encoded, sent via X-PAYWAY-HMAC-SHA512.
- API-side signing also uses HMAC-SHA512 (e.g., req_time + merchant_id + merchant_ref with the public key).
➡️ Any mention of HMAC-SHA256 in older material is legacy; the current documented algorithm is HMAC-SHA512. 4) Who configures the Customer Module callback URL (sandbox & prod)
- There is only one callback URL, and changing it “requires support ticket”.
- There is no portal self-service documented for Customer Module callback URLs.
➡️ For both sandbox and production, the callback URL is configured/changed by the PayWay team, not directly by the merchant. 5) Sandbox provisioning of Customer Module + KHQR printed-QR flow
Docs for the Customer Module and related APIs state:
- Dependencies: “Invoicing Tool or Payment Links must be enabled.”
- Customer Module uses webhook callbacks, and reconciliation via get-transactions-by-mc-ref (Customer ID as merchant_ref).
- QR/KHQR flows in general are described as being enabled first in sandbox, then in production after review. Putting this together:
- A sandbox profile can be provisioned with: - The Customer Module (via enabling Invoicing Tool / Payment Links on that sandbox profile), and - The necessary KHQR/QR services and domains.
- That allows merchants to rehearse the printed static QR / invoicing flow end to end in sandbox: portal-generated customer QR → payer scan → callback to the sandbox callback URL → fallback reconciliation.
- All of this enablement (module + KHQR + callback URL) is done by the PayWay Integration/Support team on the profile; there is no self-service toggle for the Customer Module itself. So in short: one shared callback URL per profile (all channels), HMAC-SHA512 with sorted-key concatenation as per online checkout, callback URL changes via support, and sandbox can indeed be provisioned with Customer Module + KHQR so the printed-QR flow can be fully tested.

messages.text:
Part 2/2 How to confirm whitelisting is actually configured:
- Integration Team confirmation: - Flows state that after you supply domains, the Integration Team will update the sandbox/production whitelist and confirm completion.
- Technical verification by the merchant: - For API/hosted checkout: - Calls from your whitelisted domain should succeed without domain not whitelisted or 403 errors. - Hosted checkout renders correctly from the whitelisted origin. - For callbacks/webhooks: - Callbacks from PayWay reach your endpoint from the documented IPs, and your logs show HTTP 200 responses. So practically: merchants should both keep the evidence listed above for sign-off and validate via real sandbox/prod tests once the team states that domain/callback whitelisting is configured.

Hello Bong @Ruzaid,
1) Adding/changing API and ca…
messages.text:
Part 1/2 Hello Bong @Ruzaid, 1) Adding/changing API and callback root domains; wildcards & profile scope
From the docs, the process is:
- Merchant provides to the Integration Team: - The domain(s)/IP(s) for: - API/checkout origins (where browser/API calls and Referer will come from), and - Callback/webhook endpoints. - The environment: sandbox vs production.
- Integration Team then adds/updates those domains in the whitelist for the relevant merchant sandbox/production profile and confirms back. Key documented points:
- Whitelisting is per merchant profile and per environment (sandbox and production are separate).
- Requests coming from domains not on the whitelist can see errors like "domain not whitelisted" or HTML error content.
- The HTTP Referer / origin must match a whitelisted domain. What is not specified in the KB:
- No explicit statement about wildcard subdomains (e.g. *.example.com) being supported vs requiring each hostname (e.g. shop.example.com, pay.example.com).
- No detailed self-service UI for merchants to edit the whitelist directly; all flows describe asking the Integration Team to add/change domains. So: procedure = send exact domains + environment to the Integration Team for profile-specific whitelisting. Wildcard behaviour isn’t documented and should be confirmed case-by-case with the team. ---
2) Extending or reactivating an expired sandbox profile
Docs distinguish a few sandbox-expiry situations:
- If sandbox activation link / account fails or has expired: - Coordinate with the ABA PayWay Integration Team to resend activation and ensure the sandbox account is activated.
- If sandbox keys have expired or become invalid: - Request via Digital Support official channel (e.g. digitalsupport@ababank.com) or your integration contact to extend the expiry date or issue new sandbox credentials. There is no self-service reactivation for sandbox credentials described. The supported path is to contact Digital Support / Integration Team to extend/renew the sandbox profile or keys, then:
- Log in again to the sandbox portal.
- Run at least one test transaction to confirm the profile is active. ---
3) Evidence for compliance sign-offs and confirming whitelisting
Across pre-auth, POS checkout, production onboarding, offline-KHQR callbacks, etc., the docs consistently ask merchants to retain and/or submit: What evidence to keep/submit:
- Transaction identifiers: - tran_id or similar gateway transaction IDs. - APV/approval codes, order IDs, timestamps.
- Screenshots / recordings: - Full UI flow screenshots or video for: - POS/POS-like flows. - Web checkout or KIOSK/Vending. - Mobile apps (Android/iOS) showing KHQR/deeplink behaviour.
- Technical artefacts (especially for callbacks/whitelisting): - Callback URL(s) and domains. - Browser/network logs (HTTP requests, Referer, response codes). - Server logs around callback receipt (HTTP status, payload snippets).
- Test scenarios executed: - Successful and failed payments. - Pre-auth + completion/cancel cases (where applicable). - Callback/webhook receipt vs polling, especially for offline-KHQR. These are then provided to the Integration Team during:
- Sandbox/UAT sign-off.
- Pre-auth and POS checkout approvals.
- Production onboarding and any optional call/phone verification.

messages.message:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid,
1) Rotating/reissuing a sandbox API key…
messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, 1) Rotating/reissuing a sandbox API key From the docs, all credentials (sandbox & production) are provisioned and renewed by the ABA PayWay Integration Team, delivered via secure channels. There is no self‑service key rotation documented in the merchant portal. ➡️ For a leaked sandbox key, the documented procedure is to request a new/rotated sandbox API key from the Integration Team (support ticket / direct request), then replace the key in your config and run test transactions again. 2) Overlap between old and new keys The API key lifecycle docs mention: - Keys can expire or have their expiry extended. - If a key expires, you request renewal or a new key and then replace it. However, there is no explicit statement that old and new keys are valid concurrently for a grace/overlap period. Any overlap behavior is not documented, so it should be confirmed with the Integration Team when planning a rotation. 3) Effect of API key rotation on RSA key pair & callbacks The docs treat these as separate configuration items at the merchant‑profile level:
- API key – used for hashing/signing, can expire/renew. - RSA public key – generated per profile per environment, used for signature/encryption checks. - Callback/callback URL – tied to the merchant profile and whitelisting. API key renewal/expiry flows only talk about replacing the API key; they do not state that rotating the API key will invalidate or regenerate the RSA key pair or callback registration. So, based on the docs:
- API key changes are logically independent of RSA key and callbacks. - RSA public key and callback URL remain in place unless the Integration Team explicitly changes them. For a sensitive rotation (after exposure), you can still ask the team explicitly if you also want RSA keys regenerated. 4) Temporary expirations on production keys Yes — production credential behavior in the docs:
- Production API credentials and activation links may be time‑limited during onboarding (commonly ~72 hours). - If the production key or activation window expires before use, you must request an extension or reissue from the Integration Team. - After go‑live verification, the expiry can be adjusted or removed by agreement with the Integration Team. So production keys can be issued with temporary expirations until go‑live/verification is complete. 5) Channel to notify ABA about an exposed key In this KB snapshot there is no dedicated “security incident/compliance” contact specifically for exposed keys. What is documented:
- Credential issues/changes (including expiry/rotation, whitelist updates) are handled by the ABA PayWay Integration/Operations team via their normal ticketing/support processes. - For production maintenance/changes, merchants are directed to the commercial team / digital support (e.g. digitalsupport@ababank.com). So for a key exposure, the documented path is to notify the Integration Team immediately via your usual integration/support channel (and/or digitalsupport@ababank.com), describe the incident, and request key rotation; they can then involve internal security/compliance as needed. No separate compliance-only address is specified in the docs.

messages.message:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid,
1) Sandbox TLS certificate / self-signe…
messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, 1) Sandbox TLS certificate / self-signed chain In the materials I have, there is only a requirement that merchant callback endpoints use HTTPS with a valid SSL/TLS certificate; there is no documentation about the exact TLS certificate chain used by the PayWay sandbox itself, nor any statement about self-signed vs publicly trusted CAs, certificate pinning, or future changes. So I can’t confirm from here whether the current self-signed behaviour is intended, or whether a public CA cert / published chain for pinning is planned. This needs confirmation from the PayWay infrastructure/operations team. 2) PayWay callback source IPs / allowlist range Yes, callback source IP information is documented for allowlisting:
- DC1: 103.108.218.76 - DC2: 103.108.218.2 - Optionally, you may allow the entire subnet: 103.108.218.0/24 Guidance:
- For stricter security, you can whitelist only the two specific IPs. - Whitelisting the /24 can reduce the risk of callbacks being blocked if PayWay infrastructure changes within that subnet. 3) Production callback requirements (WAF/TLS/port/location) From the documented requirements for merchant callback endpoints: - Hosting location - Merchant backends and callback endpoints may be hosted outside Cambodia (VPS or cloud) as long as they are publicly reachable over the internet and satisfy the network/security rules. - Protocol and port - Callbacks are sent via HTTPS over TCP port 443. - Callback URL should be standard HTTPS, e.g.: https://merchant.example.com/payway/callback - Custom ports like :8080 / :8443 on the external URL are not supported; if your app listens internally on another port, expose it externally via a reverse proxy/load balancer on 443. - TLS/WAF requirements (what’s documented) - Your endpoint must: - Use HTTPS with a valid SSL/TLS certificate. - Be publicly reachable (no VPN / office-only access). - Resolve correctly via public DNS. - Accept HTTP POST with the PayWay callback payload/content type. - Return HTTP 200 OK on successful processing. - Firewalls/WAF/CDN/API gateways may sit in front, but they must not block: - PayWay source IPs (103.108.218.76, 103.108.218.2 or 103.108.218.0/24 if used), or - External POSTs to the callback path. What is not detailed here:
- No explicit TLS version / cipher suite matrix for merchant endpoints is specified in this KB. Beyond “valid SSL/TLS certificate on HTTPS:443”, any stricter TLS/WAF policy would need to be confirmed with the Integration/infra team if you require a formal compatibility statement.

messages.text:
Part 1/2 Hello Bong @Ruzaid, 1) Can completion be <, =, or > original hold?
From the current docs:
- General pre-auth rule: completion must not exceed the original pre-auth amount.
- For supported card pre-authorisation transactions, PayWay can allow capture above the original hold within a tolerance of about 10% (config- and scheme-dependent). So for card pre-auth specifically:
- Lower than hold → supported (partial capture).
- Equal to hold → supported.
- Slightly higher → allowed up to ~10% over the original amount for supported card pre-auth, not for large increases. 2) When is the uncaptured remainder released?
Two cases described:
- When you complete (capture) with a lower amount, the remaining pre-authorised amount is automatically released back to the customer by the gateway after the completion is processed.
- If you never complete or cancel within the pre-auth validity window (e.g. up to ~30 days), the entire hold auto-reverses/auto-cancels and funds are released according to issuer/card-network rules. 3) Capture vs cancel race condition
The pre-auth lifecycle docs describe:
- Separate complete-preauth (capture) and cancel-preauth operations, and
- Retry/error handling and offline/manual fallbacks, but they do not define behaviour for a true race where capture and cancel are submitted at the same time against the same pre-auth. The expected outcome of that race is not specified in this KB; integrators are expected to avoid it (decide one action in your own system and ensure only that request is sent). 4) Incremental auth / re-auth support
Documented behaviour:
- PayWay does not currently expose a merchant API for incremental authorisation against an existing pre-auth (no multiple "+X" increments on the same hold).
- PayWay does not expose a dedicated merchant-facing Re-Authorisation API for continuously renewing an existing pre-auth.
- Instead, for small changes you can rely on the ~10% over-capture tolerance, and for longer/more variable scenarios the guidance is to design around Card-on-File/Credential-on-File tokenisation + new authorisations. 5) Detecting auto-release at end of the capture window
Docs say:
- Pre-auth has a validity/hold period (commonly up to 30 days; may be configured per merchant/platform).
- If not completed/cancelled within that window, the hold auto-reverses.
- There is no webhook/callback for automatic cancel or complete of pre-auth; integrations should rely on API responses and portal status checks. So yes: to detect auto-release, the intended approach is to use /api/payment-gateway/v1/payments/check-transaction-2 (and/or the merchant portal) to poll/check the pre-auth status rather than expecting a callback. 6) Issuer/central-bank constraints, refund timing, and recovering the original pre-auth for refund
From the lifecycle/operational notes:
- If online completion/cancellation or related refund operations fail due to issuer or gateway issues, you should: - Retry the online operation where appropriate, and - If still not possible, follow the offline/manual refund/cancel process via bank forms and settlement team. Those offline reversals can take time and may not immediately reflect in the portal; timing depends on issuer/card-network/operations and is not quantified in this KB.
- For reconciliation and later refunds, you are expected to: - Store and track identifiers such as tran_id (and any pre-auth reference IDs), and - Use Check Transaction API and/or the merchant portal to locate the transaction using tran_id / APV / order IDs and status. - For offline/manual correction, the docs say to reconcile using APV/order IDs and evidence (receipts, approvals) with the settlement/integration team, who can then update the status where required.

They only state that the merchant must define explicit payout amounts and ensure the sum matches their intended distribution, and that standard currency formatting rules apply. Whether ec476910 can be provisioned is not something the docs can answer; that’s up to the Integration/ops team to enable on that profile. 6) List of seeded sandbox beneficiary accounts Docs are explicit that sandbox test beneficiary accounts are provided by the Integration Team for payout testing and that real bank accounts must not be used in sandbox, but there is no embedded list of those test accounts in this KB. Hello Bong @Ruzaid, Based on what’s documented about refunds (policy, not mechanics): 1) Refund window after capture
Refunds via portal or Refund API are documented as available:
- Within a configurable online refund window, described consistently as about 30 days from the original transaction date.
- After that window, online/API refund is not available and you must use the manual/offline refund process via PayWay/merchant support (cancellation/refund form, signed by an authorized person). 2) Multiple partial refunds up to the original total
The docs state that full and partial refunds are supported (via portal and API) within the refund window, but they do not explicitly say whether multiple partial refunds against the same transaction are allowed up to the original amount. That behaviour (how many partials, remaining‑amount rules) isn’t specified here and would need confirmation from the Integration/Operations team. 3) Refund fees and who is authorized to trigger refunds
What’s documented:
- Fees: - For ABA‑to‑ABA refunds (same‑bank account payments), docs note no refund processing fee. - For some KHQR offline/manual refunds, docs say there is no fee and processing can take several working days. - For other methods, and in production generally, fees are not fully specified; guidance is to confirm with the commercial/merchant agreement or PayWay support.
- Who can trigger refunds: - Portal refunds: any user with the appropriate merchant portal permissions can initiate full/partial refunds within the allowed window. - API refunds: your backend can issue refunds using the Refund API with the merchant’s credentials/keys. - Offline/manual refunds: require a bank form signed by an authorized signatory for the merchant account (following specimen/signature rules) and processed by bank/merchant support. 4) Rounding/minimums for partial refunds
In this refund‑policy set, the docs:
- Confirm that partial refunds are supported.
- Do not restate the exact currency scale rules for refund amounts (e.g., 0.01 USD vs whole KHR) or any minimum refund amount beyond general statements like “a portion of the transaction”.
So from this material alone, I can’t definitively confirm:
- Whether partial refund amounts always follow the original currency’s scale (e.g. 0.01 USD / 1 KHR),
- Or any concrete minimum per refund (for either currency).
Those details would need to be taken from the core amount/format specs or checked with the Integration team. 5) Refunds after payout/split
The refund docs here cover standard gateway transactions (card, ABA PAY, KHQR, etc.), via portal/API and offline, but they do not mention payout/split flows at all. So I can’t confirm from this KB whether manual refund is the only path after a payout/split – that behaviour would need to be clarified with the PayWay product/ops team.

messages.text:
[Part 1/2] Hello Bong @Ruzaid, **1) Amount rules (USD/KHR, min/max, sub‑100‑KHR refunds)**
- Docs are clear on **format** for all payment operations (Purchase, QR, Refund and other payment requests): - **USD:** decimal string with **exactly 2 decimal places**. - Examples: `"0.01"`, `"0.10"`, `"1.46"`, `"2500.00"` - **KHR:** **integer only**, no decimal point at all. - Examples: `"16000"`, `"11300"`
- Do **not** include currency symbols or text inside `amount` (no `$`, `៛`, `USD`, `KHR`, commas, spaces). Currency goes in the `currency` field.
- These formatting rules apply consistently across the payment APIs mentioned (Purchase / QR / Refund); the docs treat them as **global amount rules**.
- **Per‑method minimum/maximum:** - Explicitly documented only for **USD refunds**: must be formatted with 2 decimals and be **at least `0.01`** and **not exceed the remaining refundable amount**. - Any other concrete min/max values (including for KHR, payouts, or overall transaction ceilings) are **not specified** here; they are described as limits defined by the commercial agreement / gateway configuration. If you hit `Invalid Transaction Amount`, you’re expected to validate formatting and then check configured limits.
- **Sub‑100‑KHR refunds:** there is **no explicit statement** on accepting values below 100 KHR (e.g. `"50"`) in the docs provided, so I can’t confirm whether those are allowed or rejected in production. **2) tran_id and merchant identifiers (chars, length, uniqueness)**
- For `tran_id` the documented rules are: - Max length: **20 characters**. You should enforce `length <= 20` before sending. - Allowed characters: **alphanumeric**; a **hyphen (`-`) is allowed in some integrations**. Other special characters and spaces are discouraged. - Examples of safe IDs: `"INV202510021234"`, `"ORDER-12345"` (<= 20 chars).
- **Uniqueness / scope:** - The rules state that **duplicate `tran_id` will be rejected** (duplicate transaction ID error), but they **do not explicitly say** whether that uniqueness is global or scoped per merchant profile. - So all we can rely on from docs is: **treat `tran_id` as unique for your usage; reusing the same value for a different transaction can trigger a duplicate error**, except for the special case where QR retries reuse the same `tran_id` for the *same* payment flow.
- For **other merchant references** (e.g. `return_param` / `return_params`): - Current materials do **not define strict character/length constraints**; they only state that `return_param(s)` must **not be included in the hash**. There’s no canonical max length/charset documented here. **3) Timezone for timestamps, and units for lifetime/expiry**
- **Timestamps:** - `req_time` and similar fields must follow the expected **14‑digit timestamp format** (e.g. `"20260212144826"` — `YYYYMMDDhhmmss`). - The **timezone** for these gateway timestamps is **not specified** in the docs available here, so I can’t definitively state UTC vs local; you should treat them as opaque server timestamps and confirm the timezone with the Integration team if you need precise alignment.
- **lifetime / expiry units:** - The docs acknowledge that payment sessions have an expiry window (e.g. QR sessions commonly expiring around **15 minutes**) and recommend polling `check-transaction` for up to about **5 minutes** after QR creation. - There is a `lifetime` field shown in examples (e.g. `"lifetime": 3`) but the **unit (seconds vs minutes)** is **not explicitly defined** in the retrieved material. - Likewise, generic expiry fields (QR lifetime / payment link `expired_date`) are required to be **valid and in the future**, but their **unit/zone are not formally specified** here beyond using the documented timestamp/datetime formats.

messages.text:
[Part 1/2] Hello Bong @Ruzaid, **1) Cancel / pause / resume subscription**
From the docs we have for scheduled payments:
- Subscription is **initiated** via the `subscription` flow (`token_flag=CITR_FIX`, `frequency=1W/1M/2M`).
- Subsequent charges are **merchant‑initiated** via the normal **Payment API** using the stored token (`MITR_FIX`).
- Merchants must provide UI to **“Unsubscribe – allow customers to cancel an existing subscription so no future payments will be charged.”**
- Tokens themselves have a lifecycle: `status` (0=removed, 1=active, 2=frozen) and `expired_at`. Users can **freeze/unfreeze/remove/renew** tokens from ABA Mobile, and these changes can be pushed back to the merchant via CoF callbacks. However, in this KB snapshot there is **no dedicated "cancel/pause/resume subscription" API documented** beyond general token lifecycle/CoF management. It only describes:
- Stopping your **own scheduled MITR job** for that `ctid`/token, and/or
- Relying on token status changes (removed/frozen/expired) to prevent further MITR charges. Any specific `remove-token` / freeze / pause endpoints beyond the `renew-expired-account-token` endpoint are not detailed here. ---
**2) How merchant learns about each renewal charge**
For scheduled payments, the flow is:
- Your batch job calls **Payment API** (MITR_FIX) for each due subscription.
- For **every processed payment**, PayWay sends a **payment completion callback (webhook)** to your `callback_url`.
- The documented sample pushback for scheduled payments is:
```json
{ "tran_id": "17425401324", "apv": "619195", "status": "0", "return_params": "xxxxxxxxxx"
}
```
This is the **same structure as a normal Payment API pushback**; docs do **not** define a different schema for “recurring vs one‑off” — the difference is your own context (`ctid`, `token_flag`, subscription record) and which batch call originated it. So: **yes, there is a callback per recurring charge**, and it follows the standard payment pushback format. ---
**3) Frequency vs token expiry / 90‑day rule**
The explicit 90‑day rolling expiry is only documented for **unscheduled account tokens with flags `CITI_FLEX` and `CITO_FLEX`** via the Renew Token API:
- *“Account tokens linked with the `CITI_FLEX` or `CITO_FLEX` flags will expire 90 days after their initial linking, renewal, or the last successful transaction—whichever is most recent.”* For **CITR_FIX / MITR_FIX** (scheduled subscriptions):
- Token callbacks for subscriptions include `expired_at`, `status`, `token_flag=CITR_FIX`, `frequency`, and `subscribed_amount`.
- FAQs state: *“No, expired tokens cannot be used to process payments… If a frozen or expired token is used, the transaction will be declined.”* But the docs **do not state any 90‑day rule for CITR_FIX/MITR_FIX**, nor do they say that `frequency` has any control over token expiry. They are treated as **separate concepts**:
- `frequency` = billing schedule (1W/1M/2M) for your MITR job.
- `expired_at` / token status = independent token lifecycle; if the token is expired or frozen, the scheduled MITR charge will fail. So from the docs: a **CITR_FIX token can expire**, and if it does, further charges will be declined. The exact expiry policy (whether it mirrors the 90‑day rule or something else) is **not specified** here for CITR_FIX. ---
**4) Simulating a full recurring cycle in sandbox**
In the retrieved material there is **no described shortcut to accelerate 1W/1M/2M cycles** for scheduled payments in sandbox. The sandbox notes only mention that:
- Sandbox **may** support some special test flows (e.g. token expiry manipulation) for CoF in general, and
- Standard guidance is to run your own scheduled jobs and use sandbox Payment + callbacks/Check‑Transaction for verification.

Hello Bong @Ruzaid, From the docs I have on Payment Link image support: 1) Stored image size reported as 0 There is no mention of a size field or a known issue where it’s reported as 0. This behavior isn’t documented, so I can’t confirm whether it’s a defect or expected — please check with the Integration Team. 2) Server-side constraints beyond 3MB JPG/PNG The documented constraints are:
- Accepted formats: standard image types (e.g. JPEG, PNG).
- Image width must not exceed 2,000 pixels.
- Image filename must not contain special characters such as parentheses.
Nothing is specified about aspect ratio or content‑sniffing, only the above. 3) Original filename not preserved / renamed Filename renaming (e.g. payment_link_image_<epoch-ms>.<ext>) is not described in the documentation, so I can’t confirm if that behavior is by design. 4) Hosted CDN URL stability/publicity for receipts There is no guidance in the docs on whether the stored image URL is guaranteed stable/public enough to embed in merchant-facing receipts. That aspect isn’t documented and would need confirmation from the PayWay team.

messages.text: hi @payway_Integration_AI_bot [T-23] Questions about subscription (recurring) payments via credentials-on-file — initiation works via the purchase API with ctid + token_flag=CITR_FIX + frequency (1W/1M/2M): 1) How does a merchant cancel, pause or resume a subscription — is remove-token the only documented mechanism, or do dedicated endpoints exist? 2) How does the merchant learn that a renewal charge happened — is there a callback per recurring charge, and how does it differ from a one-off charge callback? 3) Does frequency also govern the token's ~90-day renewal deadline, or can a CITR_FIX token expire mid-cycle? 4) How can we simulate a full recurring cycle in sandbox without waiting 7/30/60 days?
